passages.text: The apostles and brothers throughout Judea soon heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.
passages.sermon:
The apostles lived in Judea.
The brothers also lived in Judea.
They heard news.
They heard that the Gentiles received the word of God.
The Gentiles accepted God's message.
passages.original: Ἤκουσαν δὲ οἱ ἀπόστολοι καὶ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ οἱ ὄντες κατὰ τὴν Ἰουδαίαν ὅτι καὶ τὰ ἔθνη ἐδέξαντο τὸν λόγον τοῦ Θεοῦ

passages.text: So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, the circumcised believers took issue with him and said, “You visited uncircumcised men and ate with them.”
passages.sermon:
Peter was one of Jesus’ apostles.
Peter went up to Jerusalem.
Some believers in Jerusalem practiced circumcision.
These circumcised believers disagreed with Peter.
They spoke to Peter.
They said, “You visited men who were not circumcised.”
They also said, “You ate with those men.”
passages.original: Ὅτε δὲ ἀνέβη Πέτρος εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ διεκρίνοντο πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἐκ περιτομῆς λέγοντες ὅτι Εἰσῆλθες πρὸς ἄνδρας ἀκροβυστίαν ἔχοντας καὶ συνέφαγες αὐτοῖς

passages.text: But Peter began and explained to them the whole sequence of events: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision of something like a large sheet being let down from heaven by its four corners, and it came right down to me.
passages.sermon:
Peter was an apostle of Jesus Christ.
Peter began to explain everything to the believers in Jerusalem.
He spoke to them step by step.
Peter said, “I was in the city of Joppa.
I was praying there.
While I was praying, I fell into a trance.
I saw a vision.
In the vision, I saw something coming down from heaven.
It looked like a large sheet.
The sheet was being lowered by its four corners.
It came down right to where I was.”
passages.original: Ἀρξάμενος δὲ Πέτρος ἐξετίθετο αὐτοῖς καθεξῆς λέγων Ἐγὼ ἤμην ἐν πόλει Ἰόππῃ προσευχόμενος καὶ εἶδον ἐν ἐκστάσει ὅραμα καταβαῖνον σκεῦός τι ὡς ὀθόνην μεγάλην τέσσαρσιν ἀρχαῖς καθιεμένην ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἦλθεν ἄχρι ἐμοῦ

passages.text: I looked at it closely and saw four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds of the air.
passages.sermon:
Peter looked closely at the sheet.
He studied what was inside it.
He saw four-footed animals that live on the earth.
He saw wild beasts.
He saw reptiles.
He saw birds of the air.
passages.original: εἰς ἣν ἀτενίσας κατενόουν καὶ εἶδον τὰ τετράποδα τῆς γῆς καὶ τὰ θηρία καὶ τὰ ἑρπετὰ καὶ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ

passages.text: Then I heard a voice saying to me, ‘Get up, Peter, kill and eat.’
passages.sermon:
Peter was in the city of Joppa.
Peter was praying.
Peter saw a vision while in a trance.
Peter saw something like a large sheet coming down from heaven.
The sheet came down to Peter.
Peter looked at the sheet.
Peter saw four-footed animals, wild beasts, reptiles, and birds.
Peter then heard a voice.
The voice spoke to Peter.
The voice said, “Get up, Peter. Kill and eat.”
passages.original: ἤκουσα δὲ καὶ φωνῆς λεγούσης μοι Ἀναστάς Πέτρε θῦσον καὶ φάγε

passages.text: ‘No, Lord,’ I said, ‘for nothing impure or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’
passages.sermon:
Peter was a Jewish man who followed the law of Moses.
Peter spoke to the Lord.
Peter said, “No, Lord.”
Peter said he never ate anything impure.
Peter said he never ate anything unclean.
Peter said nothing impure or unclean ever entered his mouth.
passages.original: Εἶπον δέ Μηδαμῶς Κύριε ὅτι κοινὸν ἢ ἀκάθαρτον οὐδέποτε εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸ στόμα μου

passages.text: But the voice spoke from heaven a second time, ‘Do not call anything impure that God has made clean.’
passages.sermon:
God spoke from heaven.
God spoke to Peter.
God spoke a second time.
God said, “Do not call anything impure that I have made clean.”
passages.original: Ἀπεκρίθη δὲ ἐκ δευτέρου φωνὴ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ Ἃ ὁ Θεὸς ἐκαθάρισεν σὺ μὴ κοίνου

passages.text: This happened three times, and everything was drawn back up into heaven.
passages.sermon:
God gave Peter a vision.
God repeated this vision three times.
In the vision, God showed Peter something.
After the third time, everything in the vision went back up into heaven.
passages.original: Τοῦτο δὲ ἐγένετο ἐπὶ τρίς καὶ ἀνεσπάσθη πάλιν ἅπαντα εἰς τὸν οὐρανόν

passages.text: Just then three men sent to me from Caesarea stopped at the house where I was staying.
passages.sermon: Three men arrived at the house where I was staying.\r\nThey came immediately.\r\nSomeone had sent them from Caesarea to find me.
passages.original: Καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξαυτῆς τρεῖς ἄνδρες ἐπέστησαν ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν ἐν ᾗ ἦμεν ἀπεσταλμένοι ἀπὸ Καισαρείας πρός με

passages.text: The Spirit told me to accompany them without hesitation. These six brothers also went with me, and we entered the man’s home.
passages.sermon:
The Holy Spirit spoke to me.
The Holy Spirit told me to go with these men.
The Holy Spirit told me not to hesitate.
Six brothers went with me.
We entered the man’s house together.
passages.original: εἶπεν δὲ τὸ Πνεῦμά μοι συνελθεῖν αὐτοῖς μηδὲν διακρίναντα ἦλθον δὲ σὺν ἐμοὶ καὶ οἱ ἓξ ἀδελφοὶ οὗτοι καὶ εἰσήλθομεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ ἀνδρός

passages.text: He told us how he had seen an angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa for Simon who is called Peter.
passages.sermon:
A man spoke to us.
He described what happened in his house.
He saw an angel standing inside his house.
The angel spoke to him.
The angel said, “Send to Joppa.”
The angel said, “Call for Simon.”
Simon is also called Peter.
passages.original: ἀπήγγειλεν δὲ ἡμῖν πῶς εἶδεν τὸν ἄγγελον ἐν τῷ οἴκῳ αὐτοῦ σταθέντα καὶ εἰπόντα Ἀπόστειλον εἰς Ἰόππην καὶ μετάπεμψαι Σίμωνα τὸν ἐπικαλούμενον Πέτρον

passages.text: He will convey to you a message by which you and all your household will be saved.’
passages.sermon:
Simon, who is called Peter, will speak to you.
He will give you a message.
This message will save you.
This message will also save all your household.
passages.original: ὃς λαλήσει ῥήματα πρὸς σὲ ἐν οἷς σωθήσῃ σὺ καὶ πᾶς ὁ οἶκός σου

passages.text: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as He had fallen upon us at the beginning.
passages.sermon: I began to speak to them.\r\nThe Holy Spirit came upon them.\r\nThe Holy Spirit came upon them in the same way He came upon us at the beginning.
passages.original: Ἐν δὲ τῷ ἄρξασθαί με λαλεῖν ἐπέπεσεν τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ Ἅγιον ἐπ’ αὐτοὺς ὥσπερ καὶ ἐφ’ ἡμᾶς ἐν ἀρχῇ

passages.text: Then I remembered the word of the Lord, as He used to say, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.’
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Lord.
Jesus spoke a word.
I remembered this word.
Jesus said, “John baptized with water.”
Jesus also said, “You will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.”
passages.original: ἐμνήσθην δὲ τοῦ ῥήματος τοῦ Κυρίου ὡς ἔλεγεν Ἰωάννης μὲν ἐβάπτισεν ὕδατι ὑμεῖς δὲ βαπτισθήσεσθε ἐν Πνεύματι Ἁγίῳ

passages.text: So if God gave them the same gift He gave us who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to hinder the work of God?”
passages.sermon:
God gave them the same gift.
God gave this gift to us who believe in the Lord Jesus Christ.
I could not stop God.
I had no power to hinder God.
passages.original: εἰ οὖν τὴν ἴσην δωρεὰν ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Θεὸς ὡς καὶ ἡμῖν πιστεύσασιν ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν ἐγὼ τίς ἤμην δυνατὸς κωλῦσαι τὸν Θεόν

passages.text: When they heard this, their objections were put to rest, and they glorified God, saying, “So then, God has granted even the Gentiles repentance unto life.”
passages.sermon:
The people heard this.
They stopped objecting.
They praised God.
They said, “God has given repentance that leads to life even to the Gentiles.”
passages.original: Ἀκούσαντες δὲ ταῦτα ἡσύχασαν καὶ ἐδόξασαν τὸν Θεὸν λέγοντες Ἄρα καὶ τοῖς ἔθνεσιν ὁ Θεὸς τὴν μετάνοιαν εἰς ζωὴν ἔδωκεν

passages.text: Meanwhile those scattered by the persecution that began with Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the message only to Jews.
passages.sermon:
Persecution began after Stephen died.
This persecution caused many believers to scatter.
These scattered believers traveled far.
They went to Phoenicia.
They went to Cyprus.
They went to Antioch.
They spoke the message of God.
They spoke only to Jews.
passages.original: Οἱ μὲν οὖν διασπαρέντες ἀπὸ τῆς θλίψεως τῆς γενομένης ἐπὶ Στεφάνῳ διῆλθον ἕως Φοινίκης καὶ Κύπρου καὶ Ἀντιοχείας μηδενὶ λαλοῦντες τὸν λόγον εἰ μὴ μόνον Ἰουδαίοις

passages.text: But some of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, went to Antioch and began speaking to the Greeks as well, proclaiming the good news about the Lord Jesus.
passages.sermon:
Some men were among those who had been scattered.
These men came from Cyprus and Cyrene.
They traveled to Antioch.
They spoke to the Greeks in Antioch.
They proclaimed the good news about the Lord Jesus to the Greeks.
passages.original: Ἦσαν δέ τινες ἐξ αὐτῶν ἄνδρες Κύπριοι καὶ Κυρηναῖοι οἵτινες ἐλθόντες εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν ἐλάλουν καὶ πρὸς τοὺς Ἑλληνιστάς εὐαγγελιζόμενοι τὸν Κύριον Ἰησοῦν

passages.text: The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number of people believed and turned to the Lord.
passages.sermon:
The Lord helped these men.
God gave them strength and support.
Many people believed their message.
Many people turned to the Lord.
passages.original: καὶ ἦν χεὶρ Κυρίου μετ’ αὐτῶν πολύς τε ἀριθμὸς ὁ πιστεύσας ἐπέστρεψεν ἐπὶ τὸν Κύριον

passages.text: When news of this reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, they sent Barnabas to Antioch.
passages.sermon:
The church was in Jerusalem.
The church heard news about these events.
The church sent Barnabas.
Barnabas went to Antioch.
passages.original: Ἠκούσθη δὲ ὁ λόγος εἰς τὰ ὦτα τῆς ἐκκλησίας τῆς οὔσης ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ περὶ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν Βαρνάβαν διελθεῖν ἕως Ἀντιοχείας

passages.text: When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced and encouraged them all to abide in the Lord with all their hearts.
passages.sermon:
Barnabas arrived in Antioch.
He saw the grace of God among the people.
Barnabas felt great joy.
He encouraged everyone.
He told them to remain faithful to the Lord.
He urged them to do this with all their hearts.
passages.original: ὃς παραγενόμενος καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν χάριν τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐχάρη καὶ παρεκάλει πάντας τῇ προθέσει τῆς καρδίας προσμένειν ἐν τῷ Κυρίῳ

passages.text: Barnabas was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith, and a great number of people were brought to the Lord.
passages.sermon:
Barnabas was a good man.
He was full of the Holy Spirit.
He was full of faith.
Many people were brought to the Lord.
passages.original: ὅτι ἦν ἀνὴρ ἀγαθὸς καὶ πλήρης Πνεύματος Ἁγίου καὶ πίστεως καὶ προσετέθη ὄχλος ἱκανὸς τῷ Κυρίῳ

passages.text: Then Barnabas went to Tarsus to look for Saul, and when he found him, he brought him back to Antioch. So for a full year they met together with the church and taught large numbers of people. The disciples were first called Christians at Antioch.
passages.sermon:
Barnabas was a good man.
He was full of the Holy Spirit and faith.
Barnabas went to Tarsus.
He went to look for Saul.
Barnabas found Saul.
He brought Saul to Antioch.
Barnabas and Saul stayed in Antioch for a full year.
They met together with the church.
They taught many people.
People first called the disciples Christians at Antioch.
passages.original: Ἐξῆλθεν δὲ εἰς Ταρσὸν ἀναζητῆσαι Σαῦλον καὶ εὑρὼν ἤγαγεν εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν ἐγένετο δὲ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐνιαυτὸν ὅλον συναχθῆναι ἐν τῇ ἐκκλησίᾳ καὶ διδάξαι ὄχλον ἱκανόν χρηματίσαι τε πρώτως ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ τοὺς μαθητὰς Χριστιανούς

passages.text: In those days some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
passages.sermon: Some prophets came from Jerusalem.\r\nThey traveled to Antioch.\r\nThis happened in those days.
passages.original: Ἐν ταύταις δὲ ταῖς ἡμέραις κατῆλθον ἀπὸ Ἱεροσολύμων προφῆται εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν

passages.text: One of them named Agabus stood up and predicted through the Spirit that a great famine would sweep across the whole world. (This happened under Claudius.)
passages.sermon:
Agabus was a prophet.
Agabus was among those who came from Jerusalem to Antioch.
Agabus stood up.
Agabus spoke by the Holy Spirit.
Agabus predicted a great famine.
The famine would affect the whole world.
The famine happened during the reign of Claudius.
passages.original: ἀναστὰς δὲ εἷς ἐξ αὐτῶν ὀνόματι Ἅγαβος ἐσήμανεν διὰ τοῦ Πνεύματος λιμὸν μεγάλην μέλλειν ἔσεσθαι ἐφ’ ὅλην τὴν οἰκουμένην ἥτις ἐγένετο ἐπὶ Κλαυδίου

passages.text: So the disciples, each according to his ability, decided to send relief to the brothers living in Judea.
passages.sermon:
The disciples followed Jesus Christ.
Each disciple had different abilities.
Each disciple decided what he could give.
They chose to send help.
They sent this help to the believers in Judea.
The believers in Judea were their brothers in Christ.
passages.original: τῶν δὲ μαθητῶν καθὼς εὐπορεῖτό τις ὥρισαν ἕκαστος αὐτῶν εἰς διακονίαν πέμψαι τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν ἐν τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ ἀδελφοῖς

passages.text: This they did, sending their gifts to the elders with Barnabas and Saul.
passages.sermon:
The disciples decided to help the believers in Judea.
Each disciple gave what he was able to give.
They sent their gifts to the elders in Judea.
Barnabas and Saul carried these gifts to the elders.
passages.original: ὃ καὶ ἐποίησαν ἀποστείλαντες πρὸς τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους διὰ χειρὸς Βαρνάβα καὶ Σαύλου
